topic: Promo: one typed topic line in, one finished animated video out, what you get and what you bring
title: ONE LINE IN
ONE VIDEO OUT

script.text: Still dragging clips on a timeline at midnight?
Writing, recording, cutting, mixing, exporting, then doing it all again tomorrow.
This is for faceless creators who are comfortable with a terminal.
You type one topic line. Then the real stages run.
First, it writes the script from your line.
Next, it records the voice and times every single word.
Then it plans a shot list, cut right on the words.
Every frame is animated in code, using your own cast and sets.
The sound is built to match, then mastered to a clean level.
Every stage is a plain script you own.
And out comes your finished video. Take a good look.
You get the files you own: the engine, the cast, the sets, the scripts and the guides.
You bring your own keys for the voice and the AI writer.
No keys come inside the package, so yours stay yours.
One line in. One finished video out.
Get the full system. The link is in the about section.

science.claim: Dragging clips on a timeline at midnight is a familiar chore.
science.working: A feeling, not a statistic: no figure is stated or implied.

science.claim: The system is for faceless creators comfortable with a terminal.
science.working: The pipeline is started from a terminal command (bash run_episode.sh) and draws an animated cast, so no face is needed.
science.source: pack brief, who it is for

science.claim: One typed topic line goes in and the real stages run.
science.working: One topic line in; the stages are voice, plan, sound, render, master.
science.source: brief, what the VM does with your files

science.claim: The voice is recorded and every word is timed.
science.working: One voice call per script line builds words.json, the time of every spoken word.

science.claim: The shot list is cut on the words.
science.working: The plan step turns cues into frames; a word cut lands 2 frames before its word.
science.source: brief, plan step and cue rules

science.claim: Every frame is animated in code.
science.working: Shots are React and SVG functions of their own clock, rendered frame by frame.

science.claim: The sound is built to match and mastered to a clean level.
science.working: The sound step generates clips and places events; the master step brings the mix to minus fourteen LUFS.
science.source: brief, what the VM does with your files

science.claim: You get the engine, the cast, the sets, the scripts and the guides.
science.working: Five items, as listed in the pack brief. No count of sets is stated.

science.claim: You bring your own keys for the voice and the AI writer; none are included.
science.working: No key is inside the package; voice and writing run on the buyer's own accounts.

science.claim: One line in, one finished video out.
science.working: One topic line in, one mastered video out.
science.source: brief, what the VM does with your files
